headline: Hedge losses dent GAAP earnings as core profit jumps
summary_short: Vistra's Q2 2026 GAAP net income fell 6.7% y/y to $305M on a $488M swing in unrealized hedge losses, while Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA jumped 31% y/y to $1,767M on higher realized power prices and the Lotus plant acquisition.
summary_long: Net income fell 6.7% y/y to $305M as a $488M swing in unrealized mark-to-market derivative losses outweighed higher realized energy and capacity prices and three months' contribution from the Lotus-acquired plants. Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA, the company's core operating metric, rose 31% y/y to $1,767M on the same tailwinds. Vistra reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $6.8-7.6B Adjusted EBITDA and $3.925-4.725B Adjusted FCFbG. Balance sheet: cash fell to $435M, long-term debt rose to $19,595M, and total available liquidity stood at ~$6.3B. Vistra also committed up to $1.0B to the new Helix Digital Infrastructure venture with NVIDIA, KKR, and KIA.

drivers.explanation: Net income fell as a $488M swing in unrealized mark-to-market derivative losses outweighed higher realized energy/capacity prices and three months of Lotus-plant contribution.
EBITDA growth was driven by higher realized energy and capacity prices plus three months' contribution from the Lotus-acquired plants.
EPS fell less than net income in percentage terms because weighted-average diluted shares fell 1.8% y/y on continued buybacks, partially offsetting the net income decline.

CEO highlighted more than 30% y/y growth in Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA, 97%+ fleet availability during summer heat events, and the new Helix Digital Infrastructure investment with NVIDIA, KKR, and KIA as evidence of momentum.
